name: find-in-page-bar
title: Find in page bar
description: Find text inside a document, log or article: a small bar with the match count, next and previous, and the matches marked in the text.
docs: Pass containerRef, the element whose text is searched, and put the bar inside a relative wrapper around it (not inside the element that scrolls), and leave room at the top of the region as high as the bar: two rows on a phone, so about 7rem. A bar that is open from the start (defaultOpen) takes no focus and scrolls nothing until somebody uses it. Matches are painted with the CSS Custom Highlight API where it exists, which leaves your elements alone, and with wrapper marks where it does not (highlight="marks" forces them); the marks are taken out again exactly. Marks are real changes to the page, so about 500 matches around the current one are marked at a time and the marks move along as you step; the count always covers every match. The current match is stronger and scrolled into view with room around it, the count reads "3 of 12" in a polite live region and "No results" when empty. Enter and Shift with Enter step, Escape closes, Ctrl or Cmd with F opens it while focus is inside the region (shortcut). Case and whole word are pressed buttons, controlled with caseSensitive, wholeWord and onOptionsChange. The text is read in idle slices, so a large log never stalls typing, and it is searched again if the region changes. onMatchesChange reports the count.
